description: Idempotency vectors: a used payout ID is refused while pending, approved and after every terminal status and lapse, tombstones block reuse for good, failed and retried calls never pay twice, and request deadlines.

vectors.description: A pending payout's ID is refused on retry, whether the retry repeats the request or changes it, and the record is unchanged.
An approved payout's ID is refused on retry by the same agent and by another agent, and nothing more is reserved.
After a payout is executed, a resubmission of the same request is PAYOUT_ID_EXISTS and a second execute is PAYOUT_WRONG_STATUS, with balances unchanged.
An execute whose transfer fails changes nothing, so the payout stays APPROVED; once the recipient can receive, the retry pays it exactly once.
A rejected payout leaves a REJECTED tombstone: a retry of its ID is refused and it can no longer be approved.
Payouts cancelled by the principal and by their agent leave CANCELLED tombstones, and both IDs stay used.
A lapsed payout still holds its ID before and after a third party cancels it, and it cannot be executed.
Records outlive the mandate's expiry: once the principal extends it, retries of an executed and of an open payout are both refused.
Two years after an executed and a cancelled payout, long past any record lifetime, both IDs are still refused.
Two years on, the tombstones of an executed and a cancelled payout still read back with their status, and a new ID is accepted.
A request whose deadline is now, or already past, is REQUEST_DEADLINE_PASSED and writes nothing; a deadline one second ahead is accepted.
A request that arrives one second before its deadline is accepted.
A retry of a request that landed is PAYOUT_ID_EXISTS even after its deadline, because the ID check comes first; a new ID at the same deadline is refused.
A request batch retried whole, before and after execution, reports PAYOUT_ID_EXISTS for every item and changes nothing.
Executed payouts cannot be executed again, alone or in a batch, and the balances do not move.
A second cancel of the same payout, alone or in a cancel batch, is PAYOUT_WRONG_STATUS and releases nothing twice.
IDs are compared as raw bytes: all zero, all ones, one bit apart and a label are distinct, and a shared task_ref is no key.
A request refused by a limit writes nothing, so its ID is still free and the corrected request is accepted.
A batch item refused by a limit writes nothing, so its ID is accepted later.
